reason: Start with membrane growth, one of the three preparations needed for cell division.
expectation: I expect the phospholipids and proteins to contribute to new membrane material, though the exact construction is unclear.

alternatives.reason: Copying DNA is also necessary, but I chose to begin with the cell's growing membrane.

effect: The membrane components formed vesicles, revealing a further goal to grow the cell.
reaction: The vesicles make a plausible intermediate, though their contribution to growth remains to be shown.
reason: Combine the vesicles with the cell to pursue the newly revealed growth goal.
expectation: I expect the vesicles to add membrane to the cell surface, though how the contents grow is less clear.

alternatives.reason: Genome copying is also required, but I want to follow the membrane preparation through first.

effect: Vesicle fusion expanded the surface while protein production and organelle growth increased the cell's contents.
reaction: The before-and-after description usefully distinguishes membrane addition from growth of the rest of the cell.
reason: Copy the genome before it is shared between daughter cells.
expectation: I expect the nucleotides to be used to copy the nuclear DNA, producing a duplicated genome.

alternatives.reason: The spindle is also needed, but I chose to copy the DNA first.

effect: The genome is copied, with sister chromatids remaining together until separation; the spindle remains to be built.
reaction: The distinction between genome replication and protein production is useful.
reason: Build the chromosome-separating spindle; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect tubulin and motor proteins to form a spindle organized by the centrosomes, ready to help separate chromosomes.

effect: The spindle is built, and the new goal is to give each daughter cell a complete genome.
reaction: The picture makes clear that building the spindle has not yet separated the chromosomes.
reason: Combine the copied genome with the spindle to begin chromosome separation; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the spindle to interact with the copied chromosomes and help separate their sister chromatids, though further steps may be needed to form daughter cells.

effect: The spindle has separated matching chromosome sets, but the cell still shares one cytoplasm.
reaction: The distinction between chromosome separation and forming two cells is clear.
reason: Bring the grown cell body together with its separated chromosomes; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the cell to move toward dividing its cytoplasm into two daughter cells, although another step may be needed.

effect: Two daughter nuclei have formed, but the cytoplasm remains shared; the cell still needs to divide.
reaction: The separate nuclear and cytoplasmic stages are clear.
reason: Use the actin and myosin to divide the cell; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect actin and myosin to constrict the cell and separate its cytoplasm into two daughter cells.

effect: The cell has divided into two unspecialized daughter stem cells, completing the chapter's goals.
reaction: The final picture plan connects division to self-renewal, though it does not show how actin and myosin constrict the cell.

mostWorthwhile.text: Chromosome separation was most worthwhile: the picture plan and prose distinguish distributing sister chromatids from dividing the shared cytoplasm.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the spindle felt least informative: the picture plan shows fibres but gives little explanation of how they will attach to chromosomes or move them.

surprise.text: The membrane vesicles expanded the surface, while continued protein production and organelle growth accounted separately for the increased contents.

arbitrary.text: Combining the enlarged cell body with separated chromosome sets felt somewhat abstract because the latter was already described as a view inside that same cell. Its purpose became clearer when two nuclei formed.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the staged distinction between genome copying, chromosome separation and cell division made the constructions educational, even though the final stretch offered only one combination at each decision.
